newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Room for more gains in Venezuelan stocks -Salomon.
newsitem.headline: Room for more gains in Venezuelan stocks -Salomon.

text.p: Although Venezuela's current macroeconomic mix is probably unsustainable, high domestic liquidity combined with negative real interest rates leave room for further stock market gains, Salomon Brothers said.

"We reiterate our overweight recommendation," the U.S. investment bank said in a Tuesday market report. Salomon has Venezuela at 2.5 percent of its Latin American portfolio, compared with a one percent neutral stance.

"... the exchange rate is appreciating in real terms. In this environment, the stock market will provide excellent U.S. dollar returns providing that the local currency prices of equities simply keep up with local inflation," the report said.
"We think that this is likely, given the level of liquidity in the market and the negative real returns offered by domestic money market instruments," Salomon added.
Six month benchmark TEM paper currently offers just over 21 percent while inflation is targeted by the government to hit 30 percent for the year.

Salomon added that recent wage rises and a ground-breaking labor reform "should guarantee strong consumer demand during the second half of this year ... Consequently, firms that sell goods domestically should face a strong market."
The bank sees 4.8 percent economic growth for the year. Last month alone, the Caracas bolsa's 19-share .IBC index soared over 35 percent in nominal terms.
